package_info.package_manager: N/A (delivered via phishing, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is designed to steal sensitive information (credentials, device info) from victims, using multiple obfuscation, anti-analysis, and persistence techniques, and exfiltrates data to the attacker via SMTP. It is delivered through a phishing campaign exploiting a known Office vulnerability.

execution_context.file_location: Excel document (swift copy.xls) OLE embedded link

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the Excel document is opened, the embedded OLE link is automatically accessed, triggering a download of a remote HTA file via CVE-2017-0199.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automatic download of remote code via document open is a classic malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Excel documents should not trigger remote code execution or download files without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise documents may link to internal resources, but not to untrusted remote executables.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Obfuscated JavaScript that extracts and executes embedded VBScript and PowerShell code.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the HTA file is executed, obfuscated JavaScript decodes and runs VBScript, which in turn decodes and executes PowerShell code to download and run a malicious executable.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Multi-layered script execution and obfuscation is a hallmark of malware delivery chains.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate HTA files should not download and execute further code from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rare in enterprise automation, but never for downloading untrusted binaries.

execution_context.file_location: Decoded from HTA, executed by cmd.exe

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At script execution, downloads a malicious executable to the user's AppData directory and launches it after a short delay.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Direct download and execution of a binary from an untrusted remote server.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: PowerShell should not be used to fetch and run remote executables in normal user workflows.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software updaters may use similar code, but only from trusted sources.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Extracts, decrypts, and loads additional modules (FGMaker.dll, Q, Gammar.dll, Tyrone.dll) from resource section, using Assembly.Load() in memory.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the loader module unpacks and decrypts multiple embedded modules from its resources, loading them directly into memory to evade disk-based detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Multi-stage unpacking and in-memory loading is a common anti-analysis and evasion technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate .NET applications rarely load multiple encrypted modules from resources at runtime.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some DRM or anti-tamper software may use similar techniques.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Runs 'schtasks.exe' to create a scheduled task for persistence; renames loader file and sets Hidden, ReadOnly, System attributes.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At deploy module execution, establishes persistence by creating a scheduled task and hides the malware binary by renaming and setting file attributes.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware commonly uses scheduled tasks and file hiding for persistence and stealth.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not create hidden, system-protected scheduled tasks without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise management tools may create scheduled tasks, but not with these stealth attributes.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Performs process hollowing: creates suspended process, injects core module PE, resumes process.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At deploy module execution, creates a new suspended process, injects the core Snake Keylogger module into its memory, and resumes execution to run the malware under a legitimate process context.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Process hollowing is a well-known malware technique to evade detection and run under the guise of a legitimate process.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not inject code into other processes or use process hollowing.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rare in legitimate software, except for some advanced debuggers or security tools.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Collects device info (PC name, IP, location, timezone), traverses profile folders for credentials from browsers, email, IM, FTP clients; stores in global variable.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, collects system and credential data from over 50 software products, storing results in memory for later exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Bulk credential harvesting from multiple applications is a hallmark of infostealers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not access or exfiltrate credentials from unrelated applications.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Password managers may access credentials, but only with user consent and for their own vault.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Builds email with device info and credentials, sends via SMTP to attacker-controlled address.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After collecting credentials, constructs an email and sends it via SMTP to the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltration of sensitive data via SMTP is a common malware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not send user credentials to external email addresses.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated reporting tools may use SMTP, but not for credential exfiltration.
key_indicators: Bulk credential data in email body

attack_chain.action: Phishing email delivers malicious Excel document exploiting CVE-2017-0199.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote HTA file download and execution

attack_chain.action: HTA file executes obfuscated JavaScript, which extracts and runs VBScript and PowerShell.
attack_chain.leads_to: PowerShell downloads and runs loader executable

attack_chain.action: PowerShell downloads and executes sahost.exe (loader module) from remote server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Loader module unpacks and loads additional modules

attack_chain.action: Loader module extracts, decrypts, and loads multiple modules in memory.
Deploy module establishes persistence, hides files, and performs process hollowing to inject core module.
Core module collects credentials and device info from victim's system.
Core module sends stolen credentials and device info to attacker via SMTP.

behavioral_signatures: Office document triggering remote code execution via OLE link (CVE-2017-0199)
HTA file with obfuscated JavaScript/VBScript/PowerShell chains
PowerShell downloading and executing binaries from untrusted remote servers
In-memory .NET assembly loading from encrypted resources
Scheduled task creation with hidden/system attributes
Process hollowing (CreateProcess with CREATE_SUSPENDED, memory injection APIs)
Bulk credential harvesting from browser/email/IM/FTP profile folders
file_indicators: Excel documents with embedded OLE links to suspicious domains
HTA files with obfuscated script content
Binaries named sahost.exe, WeENKtk.exe, utGw.exe in AppData
Scheduled tasks referencing suspicious executables in AppData
network_indicators: Outbound SMTP traffic to unknown or attacker-controlled addresses
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents exploiting CVE-2017-0199, especially those with OLE links to external domains. Detect HTA file execution and chained script execution (JavaScript → VBScript → PowerShell). Alert on PowerShell downloading and executing binaries from untrusted sources. Look for in-memory .NET assembly loading and process hollowing behaviors. Flag creation of scheduled tasks with hidden/system attributes and binaries in AppData with random names. Monitor for bulk credential access from browser/email/IM/FTP profile folders and outbound SMTP traffic containing credential data.
